en.name: Panela (piloncillo)
en.summary: Panela does not spoil — sugar never does — but for best quality use a cone or block within 18–24 months, sealed and kept somewhere cool and dry. A block that has gone rock hard is still perfectly good; grate it, smash it, or dissolve it in hot water.
en.pantry: 18–24 months for best quality, sealed in a bag or an airtight tin somewhere cool and dry. The figure is borrowed from brown sugar, which never spoils either but is given the same window for quality — and panela is simply whole cane juice boiled down and set solid, so it retains more molasses and more moisture than refined brown sugar and is correspondingly stickier in a humid kitchen. The two enemies are humidity, which makes it tacky and eventually weeps molasses, and ants, which find it unerringly. Keep the cone sealed and off the floor.
en.fridge: Do not refrigerate panela. The fridge is a damp place, and damp is the only thing that genuinely damages a sugar block: it draws moisture into the surface, makes it sticky, and can set the whole cone weeping. No refrigerated timeline is given for that reason. A cool, dry cupboard is what panela wants, and if your kitchen is humid, the answer is a better-sealed container rather than a colder one.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline exists and freezing serves no purpose. Panela does not spoil in the first place, so there is nothing for the freezer to prevent, and taking a cold block in and out of a Taiwanese kitchen would coat it in condensation every time — which is precisely the damage you are trying to avoid.
spoilage: Panela does not spoil; there is no true spoilage to look for.
A sticky, weeping surface, which means it has taken up humidity — a nuisance, not a hazard.
Ants or other insects in the packet, which is the usual real loss.
A rock-hard block, which is not spoilage at all and grates or dissolves perfectly well.
tips: Seal it properly; humidity and ants are the only real threats.
Grate a hard cone, or smash it inside a bag with a rolling pin.
Dissolve it in hot water to make a syrup you can measure easily.
Do not substitute refined brown sugar one-for-one — panela has a far stronger molasses flavour.

faq.a: No. Sugar does not spoil. For best quality use it within 18–24 months, kept sealed somewhere cool and dry.

faq.q: My piloncillo is rock hard — is it still usable?
faq.a: Yes, completely. Grate it, smash it in a bag, or dissolve it in hot water. Hardness is not spoilage.
No. The fridge is damp, and moisture is the one thing that damages a sugar block, making it sticky and causing it to weep molasses.

zh.name: 黑糖磚
zh.summary: 黑糖磚不會腐敗——糖本來就不會——但以品質而言，一個糖錐或糖磚最好在 18～24 個月內用完，密封放在陰涼乾燥處。硬得像石頭的糖磚完全沒問題：磨成屑、敲碎，或用熱水化開就好。
zh.pantry: 品質上抓 18～24 個月，密封在袋子或密封罐裡，放陰涼乾燥處。這個數字是比照紅糖借來的——紅糖同樣不會腐敗，但也是給同樣的品質期間；而黑糖磚就是整鍋甘蔗汁熬乾凝固的，保留了比精製紅糖更多的糖蜜和水分，所以在潮濕的廚房裡也更黏。它只有兩個敵人：濕氣，會讓它變黏、最後滲出糖蜜；還有螞蟻，牠們找得到它的能力從不出錯。糖錐要密封，也不要直接放地上。
zh.fridge: 不要把黑糖磚放冷藏。冰箱是潮濕的地方，而濕氣正是唯一真正會傷害糖磚的東西：它會把水氣帶進表面、讓糖變黏，甚至整顆糖錐開始滲糖蜜。這裡不給冷藏期限，原因就在這裡。黑糖磚要的是陰涼乾燥的櫃子；如果你的廚房很潮，答案是換一個封得更緊的容器，而不是換一個更冷的地方。
zh.freezer: 沒有冷凍期限，冷凍也沒有任何意義。黑糖磚本來就不會壞，冷凍沒有東西可防；而且在台灣的廚房裡，一塊冰冷的糖磚每次拿出來都會沾滿結露——那剛好就是你想避免的傷害。
spoilage: 黑糖磚不會腐敗，沒有真正的腐敗徵兆可看。
表面變黏、滲出糖蜜，表示它吸了濕氣——那是麻煩，不是危害。
包裝裡出現螞蟻或其他蟲，那才是真正會讓你損失的情況。
硬得像石頭完全不算壞掉，照樣磨得動、化得開。
tips: 確實密封；濕氣和螞蟻是唯二的威脅。
硬糖錐可以用磨的，或裝袋用擀麵棍敲碎。
用熱水化成糖漿，之後就很好計量。
不要和精製紅糖等量互換——黑糖磚的糖蜜味強得多。

faq.a: 不會。糖不會腐敗。以品質而言，密封放陰涼乾燥處，在 18～24 個月內用完最好。

faq.q: 黑糖磚硬得像石頭還能用嗎？
faq.a: 完全可以。磨成屑、裝袋敲碎，或用熱水化開。變硬不是壞掉。
不要。冰箱潮濕，而濕氣正是唯一會傷害糖磚的東西，會讓它變黏、滲出糖蜜。
